END MATTER Local finite order.—Write a density coefficient as F(j) in independent metric and cut jet coordinates. Joint continuity of its differential at (j0, 0) gives neighborhoods U of j0 and W of zero with |dF(j)[h]| < 1. In the product topology, W can be chosen to restrict only finitely many coordinates. If h vanishes in these coordinates, then th ∈ W for every real t, so linearity gives dF(j)[h] = 0 throughout U. Shrink U to a basic product neighborhood and include its defining coordinates in this finite list. Jets in U agreeing on the list are joined by a straight segment along which F is constant. Thus the density has finite derivative order locally. A finite cover and partition of unity on a compact cut give a finite-order expression near each configuration. Integration by parts therefore gives a smooth local Euler– Lagrange density: graphs that agree on an open set have the same density there. At the planar jet, fix one such neighborhood and raise its finite order to include the metric sources, total derivatives and graph derivatives used below. Only finitely many coordinates are restricted by this neighborhood; higher derivatives are unrestricted.
